practical.title: Pointers & Heap Memory: Dynamic Grades Array in C (Intensive Lab)
practical.summary: An intensive, hands-on terminal lab that guides you through observing, modifying, extending, and verifying a C program that uses heap allocation (malloc/calloc/realloc) to store grades. You will compile and run a runnable starter program, make small targeted edits to explore differences between malloc and calloc, add the ability to expand the array with realloc, and verify behavior across edge cases. Emphasis: pointer usage, sizeof, allocation checks, free, and avoiding dangling pointers.
practical.sourceActivity: Pointers & Heap Memory: Dynamic Grades Array in C (Intensive Lab)

coachingPrompts: What do you predict will happen before you run it?
What evidence shows that your change worked?
Can you explain the result in your own words?

tasks.title: Scene 1 — Observe & Understand: Run the baseline program
tasks.narratorGuide: Hi — first we run the starter program to see the program flow: prompt number of grades, allocate memory, read each grade into the grades array, compute the average, then free memory. Pay attention to the allocation line and the printed average. Even though this program runs, it intentionally uses a wrong allocation expression (missing sizeof(float)). Observing correct output now (with small input) will help you understand why that line is fragile and what to change next. Next, we'll make a one-line fix to allocate the correct number of bytes.

tasks.title: Scene 2 — Modify & Experiment: Fix allocation (malloc -> correct byte count) and try calloc
tasks.narratorGuide: Great — now we'll fix the allocation to ask for the correct number of bytes. Change the one line where malloc is called so memory allocation accounts for sizeof(float). After compiling, re-run the program; the average should still be correct. Next, try replacing malloc with calloc to see how zero-initialized memory behaves if a user accidentally inputs fewer values (or to safely pre-fill memory). This small edit teaches a crucial principle: always calculate bytes with sizeof(type).

tasks.title: Scene 3 — Build & Integrate: Add the ability to expand the array with realloc
tasks.narratorGuide: Now we build new functionality that demonstrates why realloc is powerful and how to use it safely. You'll add a short interaction: after the first round of grades, ask the user if they want to append more. When they do, call realloc to resize the grades array (always assign realloc's result to a temporary pointer, check for NULL, and only then reassign to the main pointer). Update sum for newly-entered grades, then produce the updated average. This exercise links dynamic resizing, pointer reassignment safety, and memory hygiene.

tasks.title: Scene 4 — Verify & Extend: Edge cases and safety checks
tasks.narratorGuide: Excellent work! Now we verify correctness and robustness. Run tests that simulate invalid inputs (e.g., negative counts, bad grade tokens), large but reasonable allocations, and the realloc path. Confirm the program prints helpful messages and exits cleanly without memory leaks. As an extension, think about validating that grades fall within 0–100 and how you'd maintain a running median (hint: you might need a different data structure). Small experiments here cement defensive programming habits with pointers and dynamic memory.

safety.learnerWarning: This practical runs in an isolated workspace. Do not use real credentials or production resources.

cleanup.instructions: Discard the isolated workspace after completion.
